notes: 2026-10-23: this is a WireGuard VPN with open ports, not an SSH tunnel. 'Every plan is a WireGuard VPN with your own dedicated static public IPv4 in the US'; 'Connect your device with WireGuard and open the TCP or UDP ports you need from the dashboard'. The plan table is the fact the record is missing: Plus USD 2/mo gives 5 ports, 100 GB and 20 Mbps; Pro USD 4/mo gives unlimited ports, 1 TB and 100 Mbps; Ultra USD 10/mo gives 5 TB. So the record's 100 GB is the entry tier, not the ceiling, and UDP is available on every tier.

extras.transit_note: the port forwards for a user's origin and the bytes cross GetAStatic's network

interface_detail: a forwarded port on a dedicated IPv4
binding_note: the monthly byte allowance in egress.free_allowance is what runs out, and no kind in the six-value vocabulary names a byte volume over a period counted per account. per-ip-shaping is the closest, because it is the only kind that bounds a volume, and its subject here is the account rather than the caller's address
limits_note: the allowance is a byte volume over a period, which none of the six kinds names; the number is in egress.free_allowance and binding names per-ip-shaping as the nearest kind
